(छत्र), 9. Ardha Chandram (अर्द्ध चन्द्र), 10. Shakatam (शकट),
11. Ambujam (अंबुज), 12. Pakshi (पक्षी), 13. Nau (नौ),
14. Chakram (चक्र), 15. Vajram (वज), 16. Halam (हल),
17. Karmukam (कार्मुकम्), 18. Kutam (कूट), 19. Vapi (वापी),
20. Shringashtak (शृंगाष्टक).
The names of Sankhya Yogas are:
1. Veena, (वीना) 2. Vardamah (वरदाम), 3. Pashah (पाश),
4. Kedar (केदार), 5. Shool (शूल), 6. Yugam (युग), 7. Gol (गोल).
The names of Ashraya Yogas are:
1. Rajju (रज्जु), 2. Nala (नल), 3. Moosal (मुसल), 4. Srak (स्रक),
5. Sarpa (सप).
9, 10 and 8 multiplied respectively by 3, 3 and 4 give 27, 30
and 32 as the number of Nabhas Yogas in different combina-
tions of 2, 3 or 4 of the Aakriti; Ashraya etc. The Yavanacharya
has held them to be of 1800 types, but in this book these have
been dealt with in 32 essential numbers.
Ashraya and Dala Yogas
योगा व्रजन्त्याश्रयजा: समत्वं यवाब्जवज्राण्डजगोलकाद्यै:।
केन्द्रोपगै: प्रोक्तफलौ दलाख्यावित्याहुरन्ये न पृथक्फलौ तौ।। 3 ।।
If all the planets occupy movable signs it constitutes
"Rajju" (रज्जु) Yoga. If all of them occupy fixed signs it is called
Musal (मूसल) and if all the planets occupy duel signs they
constitute "Nala" (नल) Yoga. Amongst the two "dala" Yogas,
one called Srak or Mala is constituted when all the benefic
planets occupy the kendras and there is no malefic in any
kendra. These three yogas were treated by Satyacharya as
Aashraya Yogas. The two yogas Srak & Sarpa have been
mentioned by Parashara.
5. Aakriti Yogas
आसन्नकेन्द्रभवनद्वयगैर्गदाख्यस्तन्वस्तगेपुशकटं विहग: खबन्ध्वो:।
शृङ्गाटकं नवमपञ्चमलग्नसंस्थैर्लग्नान्यगैर्हलमिति प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञा:।। 4 ।।
